title: SHE NEVER AGED
subtitle: Yuki-onna, the snow woman
source: Lafcadio Hearn, Kwaidan: Stories and Studies of Strange Things (1904), 'Yuki-Onna' (told to Hearn by a farmer of Chofu, Musashi Province); yuki-onna in Japanese folklore.

lines.say: [low] He married a woman who never got older. Then one night, he told her a story... and she vanished forever.
cap: Then one night, he told her a story...

lines.say: [storytelling] Two woodcutters, old Mosaku and young Minokichi, were trapped by a blizzard in a ferryman's hut.
That night, Minokichi woke up. The door was open. A woman in white was leaning over Mosaku.
[whisper] She breathed on him. A white, freezing breath. And the old man never woke up.
Then she turned to Minokichi. [beat] But she stopped. He was young. So she made him a deal.
[cold] Never tell anyone what you saw tonight. Not even your mother. If you do... I will know.
[storytelling] A year later, he met a beautiful girl on the road. Her name was O-Yuki. Snow.
cap: a beautiful girl on the road.

lines.say: They married. They had ten children. And she never aged a single day.
[sly] One winter night, he watched her sew, and said: you remind me of something strange.
cap: he watched her sew, and said:

lines.say: [cold, rising] She stood up. That was me! I told you what would happen if you ever said a word!
cap: I told you what would happen

lines.say: [soft] But she looked at the children sleeping... and she couldn't do it.
She turned into white mist, rose through the roof... and was never seen again.
[gentle] Some secrets are promises. Keep them.
